streak.answer: Tom holds the longest regular-season win streak on file at 11 games, running from Week 12 of 2017 through Week 5 of 2018. Tony's two 10-game streaks (2023 and 2024–2025) and Evan's 10-game run in 2024 are the closest runners-up.
streak.reading: Longest consecutive regular-season win streak for any manager across all seasons (streaks run across season boundaries, ordered by season then week; playoffs excluded since game scores aren't stored).
streak.sql:
with g as (
  select mg.name as manager, s.year, w.week_number, mu.points_for > mu.points_against as won,
         row_number() over (partition by mg.id order by s.year, w.week_number) as rn
  from matchups mu
  join teams t on t.id = mu.team_id
  join managers mg on mg.id = t.manager_id
  join weeks w on w.id = mu.week_id
  join seasons s on s.id = w.season_id
  where w.week_type = 'regular'
), runs as (
  select manager, year, week_number,
         rn - row_number() over (partition by manager order by year, week_number) as grp
  from g where won
)
select manager, count(*) as streak,
  (array_agg(year order by year, week_number))[1] as start_season,
  (array_agg(week_number order by year, week_number))[1] as start_week,
  (array_agg(year order by year desc, week_number desc))[1] as end_season,
  (array_agg(week_number order by year desc, week_number desc))[1] as end_week
from runs group by manager, grp
order by streak desc limit 10

record.answer: Your regular-season record across all 13 opponents is 95 wins and 94 losses over 189 games. Your best matchup is Sean, where you're 6-1, and your worst is Tony, where you're 2-8. Your most-played rival is Dave, with 11 wins and 9 losses in 20 games.
record.reading: Tom's all-time regular-season record against every other manager, taken from the head_to_head view (regular season only, playoffs excluded), ordered by games played.
record.sql: select manager, opponent, games_played, wins, losses from head_to_head where manager ilike 'Tom' order by games_played desc, opponent

deep.answer: Jesse and John. Jesse won titles in 2013 and 2021, and John won in 2014. Neither has ever finished first in the regular season, and each has a best finish of 2nd.
deep.reading: I read "finishing first" as having the top regular-season standings rank (season_finish = 1) in any season. I counted a title as a playoff_finish of 1.
deep.sql: select manager_name, count(*) filter (where playoff_finish=1) as titles from v_teams group by manager_name

standings.answer: Russ (Captain Lamarvellous) finished first in the 2019 regular season and won the playoffs, with Jesse (Reborn A Christian) as runner-up. Six teams made the playoffs, ordered by final playoff placement: Russ, Jesse, Tom, Eric, John, and Stiv. Keeves, Dave, Evan, Tony, Brian, and Perk missed the playoffs, finishing 7th through 12th in the regular season.
standings.reading: Regular-season standings for 2019 ordered by season_finish (1 = best), showing each manager, team name, playoff team flag, and final playoff placement; playoff scores are not stored, so only placement is shown.
standings.sql: select v.season_finish, v.manager_name, v.team_name, v.playoff_finish, v.playoff_team from v_teams v where v.season_year = 2019 order by v.season_finish
